name: Kindling
description: Build ascending Fires from a moving market. Kindle chains for quadratic points and earn Sparks to choose stronger cards.
components: 40 unique suited cards, three Fires, a three-card market, Sparks.
loop: Take the first market card free, or spend a Spark for another slot. Build a rising Fire (+1 to +3) then Kindle for n² points.
risk: If the selected card fits no Fire, it Smothers the largest stack and destroys its cards. Holding a long Fire risks losing it.
caveat: Independent provisional eight-category assessment; 40-turn market drafting has strong depth but Smother is less exciting than an all-or-nothing wager. No human playtests.
evidence: Supplied agent report: 2,000 deals; depth-3 planner mean 226.56, HumanProxy 166.63, simple 100.66, random 45.84. Stats not independently reproduced in this review.
scoreBasis: Provisional independent eight-category design review (2026-10-31); psychological dimensions are predictions; supplied simulation results were not independently rerun.

name: Overswing
description: Overswing v7: 4-card hand. Start with a chosen card or flip blind; swing across zero for multipliers and bank before the pendulum snaps.
components: 40 unique suited cards; 4-card opening hand and capacity; Pendulum −10 to +10.
loop: Choose FLIP or opening STEER. Build a pot and zero-crossing multiplier; BANK after at least two card actions, scoring Pot × multiplier and drawing one replacement card if possible.
risk: Going past ±10 Snaps and loses the current pot. BANK refills exactly one card, SNAP never refills.
caveat: v7 is an experimental rules variation (4-card hand, one BANK refill, optional hand opening, two-action BANK minimum); balance and targets have NOT been independently simulated or human-tested. The displayed 8.0 design rating and reported evidence describe v6.
evidence: Historical v6 agent results: strategic mean 604.8 in 2,000 short deals; not applicable to this revised v7 engine. Local v7 automated rule/termination tests passed.
scoreBasis: Previously published provisional 8-category score for v6 only; v7 has not yet been re-rated. Do not treat v6 simulation metrics as v7 results.

name: Bondstone
description: Build a 3×3 Stone wall. Matching suits and rank runs grow your Rise; a faulty line cracks it to ×1.
components: 40 unique suited cards, 3×3 Wall, Rise 1–6, 3 Mortar tokens.
loop: Set the current Stone with two card previews. Full rows/columns are judged and cleared: suit, run, or pure Bonds score.
risk: Any Fault resets the Rise multiplier, even on a crossing row that also scores. Mortar can discard three dangerous Stones.
caveat: Independent provisional assessment; exceptionally low random baseline exaggerates the skill ratio, and risk is mostly deterministic placement pressure rather than blind wagering. No human playtests.
evidence: Supplied agent report: 2,000 deals; depth-3 mean 835.0, depth-2 655.8, simple 363.2, random 21.9. Stats not independently reproduced.
scoreBasis: Provisional independent eight-category design review (2026-10-31); psychological dimensions are predictions; supplied simulation results were not independently rerun.

name: Undertow
description: Outrow twelve Tides by breaking suits, anchoring for lasting power, and accepting dangerous Strain for bonus points.
components: 40 Crew cards, 12 Tide court cards, a face-down Hull, permanent Line.
loop: Each turn choose Break, Anchor, Row up to three cards, then retain up to four cards for the next Tide.
risk: High Strain triggers an unseen Check that may Crack, halve Catch, and destroy accumulated Strain/Deep. Surviving a live check rewards Deep.
caveat: Independent provisional assessment; multi-role hand management and Strain/Deep/Crack rules are relatively hard to teach. A no-risk planner is close to the strongest tested policy. No human playtests.
evidence: Supplied v4 agent report: 2,000 deals; MC48 planner mean 158.9 (SD 17.8), no-risk MC48 mean 147.7, random 29.4; planner Crack 8.8%. Stats not independently reproduced.
scoreBasis: Provisional independent eight-category design review (2026-10-31); psychological dimensions are predictions; supplied simulation results were not independently rerun.
